pending_qa.q: What happened when Janet McNamara asked her psychiatrist about a possible autism diagnosis?
pending_qa.r: When Janet brought up the possibility of autism with her psychiatrist, he administered a test and then told her that people with Asperger's generally have above-average IQs — implying she was not smart enough to be mildly autistic. Janet decided to let the matter go, partly because this occurred in the 2010s when the idea of an adult seeking an autism diagnosis was not as common as it is now.

pending_qa.q: Why did the label 'boyfriend' feel uncomfortable or significant to Sarah in her relationship with Ethan?
pending_qa.r: Sarah explained that putting a label on the relationship felt like entering a long tunnel — it could last a long time, which was scary. She also said that if she is someone's girlfriend, she expects to be prioritized in a certain way and to be reciprocal, and she was not comfortable with those expectations at that point. Ethan also had considerations around his 10-year-old daughter, who did not know about Sarah, and he felt that 'dad having a girlfriend' would feel very significant to a child her age.
